contexts.text: To the Angel of the Church of the Laodiceans... It here treats of the Church which places everything of the Church in bare Knowledges, and thence exalts itself above others.
They who are in evil and at the same time in good are meant by these words of the Lord to the Church of the Laodiceans...
Preface On those who alternately believe from themselves, and from the Word, and thus profane holy things, who are described by the Church in Laodicea. These... are called to the Lord's New Church.

To the Angel of the Church of the Laodiceans write () = to those and concerning those in the Church, who believe alternately from themselves and from the Word, and thus profane holy things... There are some in the Church who believe and do not believe; as that there is a God, that the Word is holy, that there is an eternal life, and many things which are of the Church and its doctrine; and still they do not believe them. They believe them when they are in their sensuous Natural, yet they do not believe them when they are in their rational Natural; thus they believe them when they are in externals, and consequently when they are in society and in speech with others; but they do not believe them when they are in internals, consequently when they are not in society with others, and are then in speech with themselves. Of these it is said that they are neither cold nor hot, and that they are to be spewed out. AR 202, Explained. AR 204.
That they believe themselves to possess in all abundance the Knowledges of truth and good... Signified.
That they do not know that all the things they know and think concerning the truths and goods of the Church do not at all cohere... Signified.
That they are devoid of truths and goods. Signified.
That they are devoid of the understanding of truth and the will of good. Signified.
An admonition that they should acquire the good of love from the Lord through the Word, in order that they may be wise. Signified.
That they should acquire the genuine truths of wisdom. Signified.
That those of them who do thus are loved by the Lord; and that then they cannot but be let into temptations, in order that they may fight against themselves. Signified.
To the Angel of the Church of the Laodiceans write = those who are in faith alone, thus who are in faith separated from charity. AE 231:2, Explained. AE 233.
In the address to the Churches in Philadelphia and Laodicea, faith according to life is treated of.

As in the things written to this last Church, namely Laodicea, it has treated of those who are in the doctrine of faith alone; and at the end there also concerning the faith of charity; to the things said above it is to be added that love makes Heaven; and as it makes Heaven it also makes the Church...
